models_evaluated: Venäläinen model 1 (revision for dislocation <6 months)
Venäläinen model 2 (revision for periprosthetic fracture <6 months)
Venäläinen model 3 (mortality <6 months)
Paxton model 4 (revision <5 years)

links.outcome: Discrimination and calibration of published models on local registry data
links.effect: AUCs 0.64, 0.67, 0.79, 0.53; all models had far from optimal calibration; model 3 largely underestimated mortality risk while the others overestimated revision risk.
links.quote: All models had far from optimal calibrated risk predictions ( Figures 2A – 5A ).

links.outcome: Calibration change after intercept and logistic recalibration on local data
links.effect: Intercept recalibration improved calibration slightly; logistic recalibration improved calibration of all models (slopes to 1.00), but discrimination did not improve.
links.quote: Logistic recalibration improved the calibration of all models ( Figures 2C – 5C ).

links.outcome: Differences between development and validation populations and variable definitions
links.effect: ASA and head diameter distributed differently between development and LROI cohorts; approach and previous surgery definitions differed; ASA differences may have prevented perfect calibration even after recalibration.
links.quote: The difference in ASA distribution may have prevented perfect calibration of LROI data, even after applying recalibration.

links.outcome: Availability of model predictors and outcomes in local registry
links.effect: 90% (40/44) of models used outcomes or predictors missing in the LROI; only 4 of 44 models (9%) could be externally validated.
links.quote: Thus, 4 out of 44 models (9%) on a TJA population could be externally validated using LROI data.

links.outcome: Model performance on external, later, population-based registry data versus development performance
links.effect: External validation showed suboptimal predictive performance in the Dutch population; discrimination was similar to development but calibration was insufficient.
links.quote: External validation of the 4 models resulted in suboptimal predictive performance in the Dutch population, highlighting the importance of external validation studies.

links.outcome: Calibration reporting in development papers of published models
links.effect: Development papers did not present calibration plots, so calibration could not be compared; discrimination was similar between cohorts but calibration poor in validation.
links.quote: Calibration plots were not presented in the development papers, and therefore could not be compared.

links.outcome: Reporting gaps in original model development papers
links.effect: Outcome definition for models 1-3 not described; baseline characteristics and AUC of model 4 development cohort not reported; unclear which previous surgeries were included.
links.quote: In the paper of models 1 to 3, the exact definition of the outcome was not described, and therefore the authors may have used another definition.

Harmonizing variable definitions across joint registries to enable model validation

links.outcome: external validation performance
links.effect: 4 models externally validated; AUCs 0.64, 0.67, 0.79, and 0.53; calibration was insufficient.
links.quote: External validation of the 4 models resulted in suboptimal predictive performance in the Dutch population, highlighting the importance of external validation studies.

links.outcome: calibration of risk predictions
links.effect: Calibration intercept/slope: model 1 –0.39/0.92; model 2 –0.30/0.97; model 3 0.12/2.24; model 4 0.08/0.50.
links.quote: All models had far from optimal calibrated risk predictions ( Figures 2A – 5A ).

links.outcome: predictor and outcome availability
links.effect: 40/44 models used unavailable outcomes or predictors; only 4/44 (9%) could be externally validated using LROI data.
links.quote: 90% (40/44) of the prediction models used outcomes or predictors missing in the LROI, such as diabetes, opioid use, and depression.

links.outcome: performance after model updating
links.effect: Recalibration improved calibration for all 4 models; slopes became 1.00, but discrimination did not improve.
links.quote: Logistic recalibration improved the calibration of all models ( Figures 2C – 5C ).

links.outcome: development-study reporting completeness
links.effect: Model 1–3 outcome definition was not described; model 4 development baseline characteristics were not described.
links.quote: In the paper of models 1 to 3, the exact definition of the outcome was not described, and therefore the authors may have used another definition.
